$comment: The tunnel kit (Tileset 04, Tunnel Systems; docs/map-briefs/tunnels/PLAN_2026-11-13.md): one structural shell a shape, material families applied to it. tools/content/kit/tunnel.mjs makes a kit tile for each family and shape (id core.tunnel_<family>_<shape>), and tools/content/tiles.mjs checks and writes them with content/tiles/core.json's. profiles: the clear opening on a cell edge every family keeps (half its width, its clear height, the top of the cap over it), so any two pieces of the same profile meet without a step. families (the first is the one MapMaker's palette shows; `preview`: a family not finished yet, named so in MapMaker's Family select; a placed piece's `family` (map format v37) picks another): materials (library materials: the masses either side, the soffit, the floor, trim, a portal's headwall and wings), lining (how the bore is dressed: haunch = a cast downstand where wall meets soffit, joints = metres between panel joints) and trim (plinth height, the floor drain, the pipe run on a straight wall, the strip light at the crown, the hazard band at a mouth, a dead end's door). shapes: arms = the sides the passage runs to; mouth = the side a portal opens to the sky (with its headwall and wing walls); door = the side of a dead end's service door; hatch = a shaft's opening in the cap [x0, z0, x1, z1]; kind = a piece of more than one cell or level (flight: one level up on steps or a ramp, buried; descent: the same open to the sky, the way down from flat ground; riser: a well between two levels; chamber: a 2 x 2 room). A family changes nothing a player or a bot collides with: trim is drawn only.

concrete.label: Concrete Tunnel
concrete.blurb: Cast concrete with panel joints, a floor drain and a strip light at the crown (utility corridors, culverts, bunkers).

brick.label: Brick Tunnel
brick.blurb: Old brick on a flagstone floor with a drain and a lamp at the crown (sewers, cellars, old works). Its arched lining and water channel come with the sewer family's own step.

shapes.blurb: A 3.6 m passage running north–south, buried: the hill stays on top of it.

shapes.name: Curve
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and turns east.

shapes.name: T-Junction
shapes.blurb: The passage runs east–west with a branch south.

shapes.name: Dead End
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and ends at a service door.

shapes.name: Portal
shapes.blurb: The mouth: a headwall, an apron between sloping wing walls (south), the tunnel going on north. It opens the hill and brings the earth to its walls by itself.

shapes.name: Stairs
shapes.blurb: The passage climbs one level on steps, from the south (low) to the north (a level up), buried: the soffit and the earth over it climb with the floor.

shapes.name: Slope
shapes.blurb: The passage climbs one level on a ramp (1 in 2), from the south (low) to the north (a level up), buried like the stairs.

shapes.name: Surface Stairs
shapes.blurb: Steps down from the surface into a tunnel a level under it: open to the sky between low walls, the tunnel going on south at the bottom, the ground at the top (north). The mouth for flat ground.

shapes.name: Shaft
shapes.blurb: A straight passage with a hatch up to the surface over its west wall, a kerb round it and its lid standing open. The ground is brought level to the hatch. It wants a ladder on that wall: the Tunnel Shaft set piece has one.

shapes.name: Riser
shapes.blurb: A capped well joining a passage (south) to one a level up (north). It wants a ladder on the well's north wall: the Tunnel Riser set piece has one.

shapes.name: Chamber
shapes.blurb: A room of 2 x 2 cells (14 m inside) on four columns, a passage-sized opening on each side: south and west in its south-west cell, north in the north-west, east in the south-east. Wall an opening you don't use (Sides), or put a Dead End on it.
